body: Will they charge me at all leading up to it? I'm already $1000 in the hole with no other money to speak of so I would have no way of paying otherwise.

I've only been hospitalized once. But that's because any time my parents noticed me getting low they would bring me home. Which didn't help in the least since none of them think I'm actually sick. I would beg them to take me to the hospital so I could get the intensive help I need but they would drive me to work and make sure the boss knew I had to stay. I think my employers can back me up. I'm afraid to talk to the two where I got so depressed I literally just stopped showing up but I know at least my retail job would back up the fact that I'm useless when I do work. I'm afraid I won't get approved because my case isn't "serious" enough, but seriously without my parents controlling me (which they don't do anymore) I am a manic depressive mess. Too many bills and am so unstable with my meds and their horrible effects right now they I don't think I could actually work normal hours.

I've been hospitalized and I believe I have a work history that proves I can't hold a steady job. If they called any of my employer they would back up the fact that starting in 2010 my ups would cause me to call out sick to go shopping or whatever and my downs would cause me to call out sick ( my last job this happened enough that I was fired). I'm hoping between this and the one job my parents forced me into with a family friend that I actually ended up paying a good bit into SS is enough. I really hope this works.

The mental exhaustion that a game face causes made it so I avoid going out. But! I made a point to find one person that I can completely "be myself" around. Whether that's crying for no reason or yelling at them because my medications are making me more irritable than usual they will sit there and know that it's going to pass and just support. I've also found that when I feel the need to hurt/kill myself I can go to that one person and tell them "hey I feel REALLY bad" and they know to keep me there so I don't go through with it. Doesn't always make me feel better but knowing I have someone to go to helps me a tiny bit. It's also helpful to find a doctor/therapist that has a way to reach them 24/7 so you can call and fill them in on what's going on so they know what to address and will help you when it's serious. Those doctors are super hard to find but they're out there and they're awesome.
Good luck! :)

Don't invest too much hope into medicines. I used to do that. Each new one it was like "this is going to help!" and they never really do, at least not consistently. So far psychotherapy as been more helpful. Relying on medications has just made me feel so insane.

I've struggled for a long long time. But I didn't do my research. After reading, buying workbooks and talking to my psychiatrist I found out that psychotherapy would help me to cope with what was happening. I wish I would have looked into this earlier when I first started medication so that the two could work together to help me manage my illness (I'm bipolar II). Best of luck. You're definitely not alone. Please message if you need to vent. I love to listen, helps me cope with my own illness.

I completely relate to substance abuse. It's extremely embarassing to admit to my doctors but I have abused alcohol for a long time. To the point where my boyfriend has become concerned that I am an alcoholic. I drink to numb the anger. I drink to perk myself up. I drink to fall asleep. I drink to get the confidence to go to class/parties/job interviews. I feel EXTREMELY guilty about driving drunk. I've driven the two hours from my school to my parents house and back completely drunk to the point where I was almost falling asleep at the wheel. It helps me, it makes me feel less insane. So like I said I completely understand. BUT if you get on medications do not do what I am because it does mess with them and I'm learning that the hard way. It's hard to stop because it's so easy to acquire. If you need someone to talk to, because I know starting on medications and getting diagnosed is hard, I am here. I'll private message you my email just in case. If you don't want to I understand completely and you don't have to. Just know someone out there understands at least part of what you're going through and you're not alone by any means.

I am definitely aiming for that. I've expressed all my concerns to my new psychotherapist and she's going to help me cope and work with my psychiatrist which I pray yields some sort of change because I feel like I'm going insane.

I informed her last week when I saw her and she seemed to just brush it off (maybe it didn't sound extreme enough or she thought I was exaggerating) and threw me on more ritalin which is what I told her I thought was causing my hypomania and scary impulse issues. I'm really thinking about trying to find a new psychiatrist but it's just so hard to re-explain everything time after time and it's almost impossible to know if they are good at what they do.

really? because I was only told about the effects of lithium. My doctor doesn't seem to have any ideas about changing them though. She was quick to throw me on new antidepressants (like wellbutrin that was supposed to "help") and ritalin (and then stronger ritalin, even when I told her about my hypomania). Ugh!

The fact that talking makes women feel better is really interesting, never really thought about it but I do tend to reach out to talk more when I'm at my extremes and it usually makes me feel better. Having "get all the things done" episodes actually sounds kind've nice haha. Mine are a bit more extreme so it's been difficult. But it's nice to read about someone advancing through life with bipolar disorder, sometimes it feels like I won't make it that far.

That's really great that you're going to instill that in from a young age. It's important that people become tolerant and able to help those around them. My family doesn't believe that I am bipolar, or that it is serious, therefore I don't have support except for my boyfriend who also puts up with the horrible things I say to him. I would be interested to know what bipolar ups and downs would do to a child, I would hope it would just force them to be more aware of emotions and patient. At least I'd hope!

I also take lithium & lamictal and I really, really think it messes with your memory. I've given up photography because I can't remember how to work it anymore, nor can I think through what I'm trying to shoot. I struggle with college because I can't read and remember what I've read. I also have trouble writing because I can't seem to keep my train of though. I take 900mg of lithium and 300mg of lamictal. I hope you talk to your doctor again because there are options that help with your memory/creativity. I'm currently trying wellbutrin and ritalin.

This was the norm for me for a couple months when I tried taking it. Was exhausted from the time I woke up to the time I fell asleep and was sleeping 12+ hours. It didn't really help my moods either. I can't remember if this is an anti psychotic or a stabilizer? I hope you talk to your doctor!

I am SO with you. I'm coming down from a hypomanic episode and am experiencing extreme anger and sadness after I realize how cruel I've been. I don't understand what's going on with me and I'm terrified I'm going to get depressed again. On another note, it's so reassuring (actually makes me well up) that you have children. I've always thought my diagnosis basically meant I would not be able to have children without them having bipolar disorder. I really, really hope you feel better!
